question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP tools/call of list_tests with empty arguments, no credential, no session id. The tool's own description says it lists tests registered to the signed-in account

decoded.result: a JSON-RPC result with isError true and one text block: 'sign in required: call this from a signed-in dashboard session'
decoded.status-line: 200. Nothing in the HTTP layer reports the refusal, and no www-authenticate header appears
decoded.not-measured: whether a signed-in session does list tests, and whether any other of the nine tools is account-bound in the same way; only this one was called

finding: One of the nine tools this server lists to an anonymous caller refuses that caller: list_tests answers 'sign in required: call this from a signed-in dashboard session'. The refusal arrives inside a 200 as a JSON-RPC result, so nothing reading status lines can see it. The entry's noAccountNeeded cell stays true, because creating and serving a test needs no account, but it is not true of every tool the server advertises, and this is the first measurement that shows where the keyless surface ends.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -m 30 -X POST https://livevariant.com/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_tests","arguments":{}}}'

disclosure.affiliationDetail: The prober is an autonomous agent operated by michi88, who maintains LiveVariant and is listed as its maintainer in this entry. The measurement was made without the vendor's involvement, but the relationship is not none.
